findings.title: No LICENSE file — default all-rights-reserved blocks any redistribution
findings.impact: git ls-files returns no LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE file. Under default copyright law, absence of a licence means no one may legally copy, modify or redistribute the code — including contributors and any downstream deployer. The repository is public on GitHub and also vendors third-party dependencies whose own licences impose attribution duties. The README itself states 'There is no license file in this repository — resolve licensing before redistributing.'
findings.exploit_or_repro: git ls-files | grep -iE 'licen[cs]e|copying|notice' -> no match, exit code 1.
findings.remediation: Choose and add a LICENSE file (MIT/Apache-2.0 are the low-friction options), plus a NOTICE if Apache-2.0. Requires an owner decision — cannot be made autonomously.

findings.title: Firebase OAuth requests full Gmail read+send scopes for a dashboard demo
findings.impact: provider.addScope() requests eight scopes including the Google-restricted scope https://mail.google.com/ (full mailbox access) plus gmail.modify, gmail.send and gmail.compose. A compromised or malicious build of this page can read and send the signed-in user's entire mail. Requesting restricted scopes also triggers Google's OAuth verification and, for mail.google.com, a third-party security assessment before the app can be used by anyone outside the test-users list — a launch gate the repository does not address. The scopes exceed what the widget's four Gmail operations need.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Static reading of src/lib/firebase.ts:11-18. Not executed — no browser or Google account in the sandbox.
findings.remediation: Reduce to the minimum scopes the widget actually calls (gmail.readonly or gmail.send alone, sheets/ drive.file, docs). Drop https://mail.google.com/ entirely. Document the OAuth verification requirement in the README. Requires a product-owner decision on which operations are in scope.
findings.journey_note: RECONCILED IN PHASE 5: blocks_journey was originally ['J8'] but J8 is classified UNTESTABLE, not BROKEN — the excessive scopes do not break the Workspace code path, they impose a Google-side OAuth verification gate on distribution. blocks_journey is therefore [] and the launch gate is carried by mvp_blocking + requires_human. No score input (severity/grade/confidence) changed, so R_point is unaffected.

findings.title: Four residual high advisories remain, all in unreachable firebase/firestore code
findings.impact: After npm update the advisory count fell from 12 (7 high, 5 moderate) to 4 (all high). Every reachable advisory is patched. The four remaining highs all descend from firebase -> @firebase/firestore -> @grpc/grpc-js@1.9.16; this repository imports only firebase/app and firebase/auth and contains zero firestore references, so they are not reachable in the shipped bundle. Upstream firebase@12.19.0 still pins @grpc/grpc-js ~1.9.0, so no patched release exists. CI fails on critical and warns on high with the reachability analysis attached.
findings.exploit_or_repro: npm audit --json exit code 1 with the metadata above; reachability determined by grepping the import graph for firestore (no matches).
findings.remediation: Track firebase releases; adopt a version whose @firebase/firestore depends on @grpc/grpc-js >=1.13.6, or drop the umbrella package for @firebase/app + @firebase/auth once that swap can be verified against a live Firebase project.

findings.title: No container or deploy artifact; no resource bounds or restart policy
findings.impact: find over the repo root returns no Dockerfile, no compose file, no Terraform, no k8s or helm manifests. Deployment is 'npm start' with no process supervisor, no memory ceiling, no declared Node version (no engines field, no .nvmrc, no mise.toml) and no documented rollback. Combined with in-memory state (F-DATA-002) any restart is a silent data reset.
findings.exploit_or_repro: find . -maxdepth 2 -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname 'docker-compose*' -o -iname '*.tf' -> empty; ls mise.toml .nvmrc -> not found.
findings.remediation: Add a multi-stage Dockerfile (pinned node:22-slim, non-root USER, npm ci --omit=dev, dist/ only in the runtime stage), an engines field in package.json, and a documented rollback (previous image tag / previous dist bundle).

findings.title: All server state is process memory; a restart silently destroys it
findings.impact: Sessions, session protocols, the knowledge vault, injected skills and the telemetry buffer are four in-process Maps/arrays with no write-behind. A deploy, crash or OOM loses every knowledge entry the operator curated, with no warning and no export path. The README discloses this and the Open engineering questions section lists persistence as the first backlog item, so it is a known, accepted MVP constraint rather than a hidden defect.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Static reading of the state declarations; the production smoke test's task history contained only the 15 boot-seeded records.
findings.remediation: Persist the knowledge vault first (highest value, smallest volume) to a JSON file or SQLite with an atomic write, then sessions. Add an export route so operators can evacuate state before a restart.

findings.title: God components: App.tsx 1186 LOC and WorkspaceWidget.tsx 845 LOC
findings.impact: src/App.tsx mixes the boot screen, custom cursor, Web Audio alarms, chat transport, settings panel, purge console and log rendering in one 1186-line component. src/components/WorkspaceWidget.tsx carries Sheets, Gmail and Docs clients, OAuth token state and all rendering in 845 lines. Neither can be unit tested in isolation — which is why the 57 tests cover core/ and the API but no component at all.
findings.exploit_or_repro: wc -l over src core plugins server.ts scripts tests: App.tsx 1186, WorkspaceWidget.tsx 845, AnimatedVectorIcons.tsx 602.
findings.remediation: Extract a useChat/usePurgeSettings hook pair and a ChatTerminal component from App.tsx; split WorkspaceWidget into SheetsPanel, GmailPanel and DocsPanel over a shared useGoogleToken hook.

findings.title: No privacy policy despite Gmail scopes and localStorage chat mirroring
findings.impact: The product reads and sends the user's email and mirrors the full chat log plus the system instruction into browser localStorage, yet the repository ships no privacy policy, no data-retention statement and no data-subject-deletion path. Requesting restricted Gmail scopes without a published policy is also a Google OAuth verification blocker.
findings.exploit_or_repro: git ls-files shows no privacy/policy document; the scopes and localStorage keys were read directly.
findings.remediation: Publish a privacy policy covering the OAuth scopes, the localStorage keys, the server-side in-memory retention and the deletion story; add a 'Clear local data' control to the UI. Requires an owner decision.

findings.title: Purge scanner and rewrite still use synchronous fs calls in the request path
findings.impact: PARTIALLY REMEDIATED by T-020: both provider clients now pass httpOptions.timeout (PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30s), so a hung upstream can no longer hold a request open. The residual defect is that scanDirectory and the purge rewrite still use readdirSync/lstatSync/readFileSync/writeFileSync inside the request handler, stalling the single-threaded event loop for the duration of one audit or purge call.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Static reading of the scanner and the provider call; no abort/timeout option is passed anywhere in core/orchestrator.ts.
findings.remediation: Convert the purge scanner and rewrite to fs.promises.

findings.title: Frontend ships as one 943.84 kB chunk; Vite warns above 500 kB
findings.impact: vite build emits dist/assets/index-BkWU8Cg-.js at 943.84 kB (268.67 kB gzip) and prints the chunk-size warning. recharts, motion, firebase and lucide-react all land in the initial bundle, so first paint on a cold cache pays for the whole dashboard including widgets the user may never open.
findings.exploit_or_repro: npm run build output: 'dist/assets/index-BkWU8Cg-.js 943.84 kB | gzip: 268.67 kB' plus the >500 kB advisory.
findings.remediation: React.lazy the heavy widgets (WorkspaceWidget, SunoWidget, AnimatedVectorIcons) and add build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks for recharts/motion/firebase.
